gap: No result ChatGPT got states a named latency measurement for a 75% 8K magnetic board under $100: HLPlanet (Marcus Richardson, OSLTT, 2026-05-18) measured the Gamakay TK75 TMR at 0.60 ms wired and 0.75 ms on 2.4 GHz, next to 0.5 ms in HLPlanet's table for the MonsGeek FUN60 Ultra.
standout_why: Compared against gamepadsquire (cited), setupinsider, mechanicalkeyboard.net, HLPlanet's Hall effect guide and the RTINGS best-keyboards page. The first three carry maker specs only, with no measured latency and no named tester; mechanicalkeyboard.net says so itself ('Polling rates are manufacturer specifications'). HLPlanet's guide has OSLTT figures for boards ChatGPT did not pick (MCHOSE Ace 68 0.3 ms, Wooting 80HE 0.42 ms) and none for the TK75 TMR, TK75HE V2, NS75, NS68, Ace 60 Pro, HE68 Lite, HE80 or K673 HE. The RTINGS best-keyboards page gave me a model list only. Two cited pages went unread: keebforce.com failed on a certificate error and the PC Gamer guide body was truncated, so I can't rule out that either has a figure. Not a 3 because RTINGS's own latency numbers for the Ace 60 Pro and FUN60 Ultra are behind its membership wall, so the side-by-side is incomplete.
decides: It does not overturn ChatGPT's 60% picks. RTINGS, in words, rates both the MCHOSE Ace 60 Pro and the MonsGeek FUN60 Ultra (TMR wireless unit) as having remarkably low latency, and HLPlanet's table puts the FUN60 Ultra at 0.5 ms. It does give the Gamakay TK75 TMR an honest segment: of the 75% boards in play (Epomaker HE80, Redragon K673 HE, Yunzii RT75 Pro, Gamakay NS75 and TK75HE V2), it is the only one I found with a named sub-1 ms measurement, and the only one measured on 2.4 GHz (0.75 ms). That supports it as the 75% wireless pick while its sale price holds under $100 (Gamakay's sale ends 2026-11-30). No named measurement turned up for the HE68 Lite, HE80, K673 HE, NS75, NS68 or TK75HE V2, so their 8K and latency numbers stay maker ratings. HLPlanet's guide also lists the Yunzii RT75 Pro as '1000Hz polling, wired only', which conflicts with the 'Dual 8K Wireless' listing ChatGPT showed; check Yunzii's own page before that row is used.

findings.label: Measured latency, wired (HLPlanet, OSLTT)
findings.note: Review by Marcus Richardson dated 2026-05-18: 'I tested the keyboard with OSLTT (Open Source Latency Testing Tool).' The review quotes $119.99 at the time; that is not today's price.

findings.label: Measured latency, 2.4 GHz dongle (HLPlanet, OSLTT)
findings.note: Same review and tool. 0.75 − 0.60 = 0.15 ms added by the dongle. No Bluetooth latency is reported. The spec table lists 8,000 Hz wired and 2.4 GHz and 1,000 Hz Bluetooth, but the review does not say polling was measured per mode.

findings.label: RTINGS latency verdict (figures behind membership wall)
findings.value: 'Remarkably low single-key and multi-key latency performance'; 4-chord split delay 'somewhat underwhelming'
findings.note: RTINGS: 'We bought and tested a wireless configuration with TMR sensors.' Latest changelog entry is 'Updated Oct 30, 2026'. The page confirms 8,000 Hz maximum polling. The millisecond values showed as locked; I read the page text through the r.jina.ai reader because the direct fetch returned navigation only. The unit tested is the TMR wireless version, not the $59.99 wired HE version ChatGPT showed at Micro Center.

findings.label: RTINGS latency verdict (figures behind membership wall)
